name: READXREF.jcl
description:
The JCL job **READXREF** executes program **CBACT03C** to read and process the Card Cross-Reference VSAM file, which maps relationships between card numbers and account information. The job runs as a single step, reading the cross-reference data in shared mode to support card-to-account lookup operations.Key Functionalities:
Reads the Card Cross-Reference VSAM KSDS file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDXREF.VSAM.KSDS) in shared mode to access card-to-account cross-reference records
Processes cross-reference data linking credit card numbers to their associated account identifiers
Produces output reports/listings directed to system output (SYSOUT and SYSPRINT) reflecting the cross-reference file contents

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference master file (CARDXREF VSAM KSDS) is available and accessible in shared read-only mode, containing credit card number-to-account number mapping records, AND the CBACT03C program is available in the CardDemo application load library
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The READXREF job is submitted and STEP05 is triggered to execute the Card Cross-Reference reading program (CBACT03C) unconditionally with no pre-conditions or dependencies on any prior step
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program CBACT03C reads all card-to-account cross-reference mapping records from the Card Cross-Reference VSAM file, generates a formatted listing report of those cross-reference records to the SYSPRINT print queue, and writes processing status messages (such as record counts and any exceptions encountered) to the SYSOUT system output queue — with no modifications, deletions, or additions made to the source Card Cross-Reference file

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - CBACT03C - Card Cross-Reference File Reading and Reporting
rules.Rule_Description: This step invokes the Card Cross-Reference reading program (CBACT03C) to read all card number-to-account number mapping records from the Card Cross-Reference master file and produce a formatted report listing. The file is accessed in read-only shared mode, ensuring no data is modified during the process. All report output is directed to the system print queue and all processing status messages are directed to the system output queue.
